set.st: About 1849 ('about 25 years' before 1874) John McArdill, a jewellery pedlar from London, Canada, was robbed of $4,000-5,000 in coin, watches and jewellery. A deathbed letter from the thief, dated 12 Sep 1873 and postmarked Branch County, said the loot was in a dry well on the south side of the Kalamazoo River in the Newbre neighbourhood, at a stated distance from the old graveyard and about eighty paces from the road, the well filled with oak stumps. The well was found on N. A. Burton's lot as described. On 10 Sep 1874 McArdill's diggers hit the stumps about 40 ft down, and on 24 Sep the Detroit News reported that he 'has got to the bottom of his well at last, and has found no treasure … a disappointed and disgusted man.' By late October 'the belief has become almost universal' that McArdill got the money on the last day: a neighbour said the diggers had not reached bottom when he went to dinner and were hastily filling the hole when he came back. Pin is the half-mile stake the letter paced from, not the well itself.
set.t: Dug to the bottom in Sep 1874 with nothing reported found; the Jackson Citizen (29 Oct 1874) carried the local rumour that McArdill quietly got it. The letter put the well under half a mile N of the gravel road and about 8 paces from the N-S road; the correspondent paced 80 to the road and 155 to the half-mile stake, so the well lies beside the 27/28 road within about 120 m of the W quarter corner. Private farmland: ask permission.
pinev: 1873 plat: N. A. Burton 160 = NW¼ sec 27 T2S R7W; Newbre farms across the S-line road; letter's paces put the well within ~120 m of the W quarter corner beside the 27/28 road.
W quarter corner from BLM PLSS (42.26852,-85.12030); the 27/28 road still shows on 2017 Michigan 1 m lidar; dry farmland.

The 1873 plat shows the graveyard at the SW corner of sec 27, matching the letter's graveyard reference; the well lies between it and the W quarter corner along the 27/28 road, nearer the quarter corner by the paces.
set.n: Pedlar McArdill's robbery gold, dry well in the Newbre neighbourhood, Emmett Twp (c.1849 robbery; 1874 dig)
set.y: robbed c.1849; well dug Sep 1874, nothing found; recovery rumoured
